norms.text: A body leaves the Rose's hands only under the shelter, never on the road.
Every carriage charge is written in the book before the bundle is wrapped.
Bones brought to the dirt near a tree can still go home.

taboos.text: Handing over a body without its tag.
Haggling over the charge in front of the dead.

values.text: A tag on every basket and a line in the book for every coin.

contempts.text: Anyone who calls the charge a ransom inside the shelter.

place.text: A shelter, a hut and a brazier on a dry rise where the dead change hands.

work.text: The Rose releases the dead, the Chainbreakers pay, the carrier takes them home.

danger.text: Death hoppers in the wet ground below the rise; a wisp after dark.

rumour.text: A tag came back for a person seen alive.

directions.text: Ways are given by the Prison road: the Rose one way, the villages the other.

addressTerms.text: Stranger, to anyone who has not come for a body.

neverSaid.text: The word ransom, inside the shelter.

grievances.text: The carriage charge is the most resented coin in the south. Both sides need it paid.

rumours.text: A bone-tag came back for a person who is alive.

views.text: The villages wait at home for what the carrier brings.

dissent.text: He wraps and carries bodies the Rose would not let go without coin; he sees the families at their worst (record notes).
